stories.headline: How Team USA rallied to beat France and win World Cup gold
stories.summary: France led by 14 points early, but the U.S. defense dominated and veterans stepped up to capture a fifth straight gold.
stories.body:
The U.S. women's basketball team has not lost a game in major international play since 2006 and has lost only one gold medal game (in 1983). Yet when the Americans faced a double-digit deficit in the first half of the FIBA Women's World Cup final Sunday, they couldn't just rely on history.

They had to get it done on court.

Team USA beat France 97-79 in Berlin to win its fifth consecutive World Cup title and 12th overall. Trailing 45-43 at halftime, the Americans took control in the third quarter, outscoring France 30-12. That dominance decided the game and the gold medal.

Coming in, France had been the more impressive team in the tournament, winning its five games by an average of 35.6 points with no margin closer than 22. Team USA, by contrast, beat Italy in group play by three points and Spain in the semifinals by 10. A strong start Sunday kept the momentum on France's side.

But then the U.S. defense took it up a notch in the second half, and the offense followed. The mojo changed entirely in the Americans' favor, with multiple players stepping forward.

Stars such as four-time WNBA MVP A'ja Wilson and Kelsey Plum were out due to injuries. That led to seven of the 12 U.S. players competing in their first major 5-on-5 international competition, including Rhyne Howard, Aliyah Boston, Caitlin Clark and Paige Bueckers, the past four WNBA Rookie of the Year award winners.

But the veterans supplemented all the "new," led by Jackie Young, Breanna Stewart, Chelsea Gray, Kahleah Copper and Napheesa Collier. Young, who had 18 points, six rebounds and five assists, was Sunday's player of the game. Stewart, who had 22 points, 10 rebounds and four assists, was MVP of the tournament.

Now the WNBA players from all the teams in this tournament head back to finish the regular season and get ready for the playoffs. But here's how Team USA stayed on top of the world and denied France its first World Cup gold.

How did Team USA go from trailing by 14 points to winning by 18?

Voepel: Defense. France was getting the shots it wanted and making them in the first half. That had been the case throughout this tournament, as the French offense had controlled all its previous games.

That changed in the second half, as the U.S. women relied on both their individual defensive strengths and their ability to switch without losing anything in their matchups. Everything the Americans did in the third quarter defensively was sharper, quicker and more focused. Not surprisingly, forcing France into missed shots and turnovers fueled the Americans' offense.

U.S. coach Kara Lawson is known as a defensive coach at Duke, and U.S. assistant Natalie Nakase guides the WNBA's top defensive team, the Golden State Valkyries. That expertise on the bench and the defensive strengths of the Americans' veterans turned around the game.

Stewart told TNT after the game that even when the Americans were down 14, they really weren't rattled. The fact that they cut the deficit to two by halftime -- a big steal by Angel Reese led to a 3-pointer by Clark before the buzzer -- gave the team a boost. And the Americans looked very confident starting the third quarter. Those 10 minutes made all the difference.

Philippou: Lawson said the second quarter might have been her favorite of the game. The U.S. women still trailed by two when the period ended, but the momentum had shifted in their favor -- especially after those plays from Reese and Clark -- and they had started to figure out some things. Once they got into the locker room, they could home in on how to fix the defensive lapses that plagued them early on.

At halftime, Stewart said, Lawson told the players that France might stay with them for three quarters, but by the time they got to the fourth, the United States was going to be able to bust things open. "Little do we know," Stewart said, "it came in the third quarter."

And before long, Team USA looked to have regained the psychological edge, getting whatever it wanted on both ends. Another back-breaking moment was when France got called for two flagrants in a single play at the end of the third quarter, which resulted in a five-point possession for the United States and extended its lead to 73-57 going into the fourth.

"We have to give France a lot of credit," Clark said. "They play with a lot of grit. They play with a lot of passion. They're aggressive. But I think we showed what wearing a USA jersey is all about. It's about dominating, and that's exactly what we did."

Did it hurt that France wasn't tested until the gold medal game?

Voepel: This wasn't a tight game down to the wire in which France might have needed that experience. However, where it perhaps cost the French is that they hadn't faced a defense as good as what Team USA threw at them in the third quarter. France had been especially good all tournament from behind the arc, and it again reached double-digit 3-pointers with 11 on Sunday. But the French went from 8-of-14 from 3-point range in the first half to 3-of-10 in the second.

And Gabby Williams, who had been a force all tournament, went from 16 points in the first half to four in the second. Marine Johannes, one of France's main sharpshooters, had just one 3-pointer in the game.

How well did Team USA's newcomers play?

Voepel: Overall, they did their jobs, and that says a lot when you add in the extra pressure of playing for your country. Tons of eyes were on Clark, of course, and she had a double-double in Team USA's opener vs. China. While she didn't shoot as well from 3-point range as she would have liked during the tournament (7-for-25, 28%), she was 2-of-3 from behind the arc Sunday and 4-of-5 from the field. She finished with 12 points and three assists and led Team USA in overall assists for the tournament with 32. Reese also made her presence felt, especially on the defensive end of the court where her size and quick hands flustered foes.

Guards Clark and Bueckers don't have anywhere near as much experience at the international level or in playing together as Gray and Young, who have been Las Vegas Aces teammates for six years with three WNBA titles. That helps explain why Lawson relied more on the vets during the most stressful periods in the Americans' close games but gave the youngsters playing time throughout the tournament so that the vets weren't worn out by the gold medal game.

Every Team USA basketball coach -- women's and men's -- is always heavily scrutinized for how they balance having so much talent and distributing minutes. In the end, give Lawson credit for how she allowed growth and important court time for the young players but also understood when veteran experience was what Team USA needed most.

Philippou: Taking the tournament as a whole, all of the young players had some really strong moments, showed where they have some room for growth and demonstrated the promise of what they might be able to do over time as a collective. And while Lawson relied heavily on the vets against France, what those younger players absorbed from the experience of playing for the senior national team and observing the older players is invaluable. With Team USA coming home with gold and its winning streak in major international tournaments intact, it was as good of a debut as could realistically be expected.

What does this win mean for Team USA?

Voepel: It's a new era for the world's dominant power in women's basketball but the same result. Team USA's last loss in a major international competition was in the 2006 World Cup semifinals to Russia. Before that, the most recent American losses were in the 1992 Olympic semifinals to what was then called the Unified Team (essentially the former Soviet Union with an interim name) and the 1994 World Cup semifinals to Brazil.

While we already noted Team USA's only major competition loss in a gold medal game came in the 1983 World Cup to the Soviet Union, the Americans have one other silver medal. That came in the 1976 Olympics, the first time the Summer Games had women's basketball. But that was a six-team round-robin tournament that the Soviets won by going 5-0. Team USA was 3-2 but took silver thanks to its round-robin win over fellow 3-2 team Bulgaria.

All that history is important to illustrate how outstanding Team USA has been in the Olympics and World Cup and to show what an upset it would have been had France taken the gold Sunday. It would have been just the third silver for Team USA.

All these World Cup players could be back in the mix for the 2028 Olympics in Los Angeles, along with Wilson, Plum and up-and-coming younger standouts such as WNBA rookie Olivia Miles and college stars such as JuJu Watkins, Sarah Strong and Hannah Hidalgo. The pipeline for talent continues to be full.

Philippou: And yet the tournament reminded us that winning is hard, even as USA Basketball often makes it look easy, and it's getting even more difficult as the quality of play and teams improves globally.

Sue Bird, the managing director for the U.S. women's national team, made an interesting point in a pregame news conference: With more international players coming to the WNBA and getting plenty familiar with the Americans, the psychological factor of being intimidated by Team USA on a World Cup or Olympic stage won't be as prevalent. The United States won't be able to rest on its laurels if it wants to continue its run of dominance, and it'll be interesting to see how the U.S. women continue to evolve and grow.

What does the loss mean for France?

Voepel: The French wanted this very badly and played great for 5½ games in this tournament. But the second half Sunday was like the clock striking midnight on France's hopes. The French just couldn't match Team USA when the Americans went to their next gear. That said, look at the progress France has made internationally and in the WNBA; 13 French players have been on WNBA rosters this season. The sky is the limit for a youngster like Seattle Storm center Dominique Malonga (21 points, six rebounds Sunday). France lost by just one point to the United States in the 2024 Olympic final in Paris and now takes silver in the World Cup.

Add that to Spain's bronze medal and host Germany's fourth-place finish, and it's an excellent showing for Europe, whose players have become a significantly bigger factor in helping the WNBA improve its talent level and global footprint. Plus, France and the rest of Europe will be all the more motivated for the Los Angeles Games in two years.

stories.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Man United, Bruno Fernandes contract talks stall
stories.summary: Manchester United want to retain Bruno Fernandes and have begun talks over a new contract. Transfer Talk has the latest.
stories.body:
Manchester United want to retain Bruno Fernandes and have begun talks over a new contract, while Barcelona left back Alejandro Balde could be available in January.

Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Manchester United are in talks with midfielder Bruno Fernandes regarding a new contract, transfer journalist Fabrizio Romano reports. United are believed to be keen to secure the 32-year-old to a new deal at Old Trafford following interest in the summer from Galatasaray as well as clubs in Europe and Saudi Arabia, but negotiations are taking extra time as discussions continue over clauses and potential bonuses. Fernandes has started all six matches for Man United this season, scoring his fourth goal of the campaign in the 4-0 Champions League win over Sabah.

- Barcelona are preparing to offload left back Alejandro Balde, according to Diario Sport. It is reported that manager Hansi Flick plans to use both Xavi Espart and João Cancelo ahead of the 22-year-old, and the Blaugrana would be willing to accept offers in the region of €40 million if they receive a proposal in January. Balde, who made 28 La Liga appearances last season, has previously been linked with Manchester United, Liverpool, and Inter Milan.

- Atletico Madrid are challenging Tottenham Hotspur and Nottingham Forest in the race for Athletico Paranaense defender Arthur Dias, TEAMtalk reports. The 19-year-old is reportedly attracting interest from multiple clubs across Europe, which has increased following his call-up by manager Carlo Ancelotti to the Brazil senior national team. He remains contracted with the Brasileirao side until December 2028, but his club are ready to begin talks over a new contract to fend off interest in his signature.

- Bayern Munich aren't considering a move for Manchester City attacking midfielder Rayan Cherki, Bayern insider Christian Falk reports. It is said that the 23-year-old was never on the Bundesliga champions' shortlist despite reports indicating they were lining up an approach for him. They reportedly could explore the transfer market for a winger should they need to find a replacement for Serge Gnabry or if uncertainty grows over the future of Michael Olise, who is contracted at the Allianz Arena until the summer of 2029.

- Chelsea are weighing up a fresh approach for Monaco midfielder Lamine Camara, according to Football Insider. The Blues remain interested in the 22-year-old despite belief that they will need to repair their relationship with the Ligue 1 club, who cancelled his proposed switch to Stamford Bridge on deadline day. Xabi Alonso remains intent on strengthening in midfield following the departure of Enzo Fernández to Manchester City, but there could be competition in any future move for Camara amid links to Liverpool.

Other rumors
- Juventus and Atletico Madrid are exploring a potential loan move in January for Arsenal winger Noni Madueke. (Caught Offside)

- Brighton are set to ward off interest in midfielder Yasin Ayari, who is on the radar of several clubs in Europe. (Football Insider)

- Crystal Palace are keen to sign goalkeeper Dean Henderson to a new contract. (The Athletic)

- Newcastle want to keep hold of defender Dan Burn with belief that his experience can benefit the squad. (Caught Offside)

- Getafe have received an approach from the representatives of free agent midfielder Renato Sanches regarding potential interest in signing him. (Fabrizio Romano)

- Lazio manager Gennaro Gattuso isn't keen on free agent striker Mauro Icardi amid links to the Serie A club. (Corriere dello Sport)

- Napoli and Como are looking at Stade Rennais midfielder Sebastian Szymanski. (Ekrem Konur)

- BSC Young Boys midfielder Alvyn Sanches is attracting interest from Lille and Fiorentina. (Ekrem Konur)

stories.headline: NBA offseason recap, early 2026-27 season previews by team
stories.summary: We're looking back at the offseason and taking an early look at the regular season by rolling out one team profile each weekday through Sept. 18.
stories.body:
After an eventful July full of big trades, intriguing signings and the game's biggest star shocking everyone by heading East, the NBA offseason is nearly complete. And with the regular-season schedule now out, it's time to start thinking about the 2026-27 season.

ESPN's staff of experts is looking back at the offseason and taking an early look at the season for all 30 teams, with 30 pieces -- one for every team -- rolling out each weekday through Sept. 18. We're answering the biggest looming questions, evaluating X factors and much more for every team.

Check out the rollout schedule below, with stories added daily:

Quick links:

Free agency buzz | FA grades | Trade grades

Transactions | Schedule | More NBA coverage

Atlantic Division

Philadelphia 76ers: Sept. 14
Key additions: F LeBron James, G Jaylen Brown, G Anfernee Simons, F Dean Wade, G Labaron Philon Jr., G Kentavious Caldwell-Pope

Key subtractions: F Paul George, C Andre Drummond, G Quentin Grimes, G Kelly Oubre Jr.

No team changed its fortunes from April to July as drastically as the 76ers. Taking advantage of Boston's desire to get out of the Jaylen Brown business enabled it to accomplish so much: getting a motivated All-Star feeling the sting of rejection following a career year, dumping George's contract and putting themselves in position to be attractive to an all-time great in James, who was looking for a new challenge. They also lessened their dependency on Joel Embiid's bothersome health as he will turn 33 during the season.

They filled in the blanks by adding Caldwell-Pope and Wade as plug-and-play wings, changing the complexion of their franchise in several swoops. If nothing else, they won the offseason. -- Vincent Goodwill

Read the full offseason recap/season preview

Boston Celtics: Sept. 15
Key additions: Paul George, Mitchell Robinson, Mike Conley

Key subtractions: Jaylen Brown, Nikola Vucevic

Key retentions: Neemias Queta, Jordan Walsh, Ron Harper Jr.

Boston responded to its first early playoff exit since 2021 by boldly trading Brown to the 76ers, ending his fruitful partnership with Jayson Tatum. The move should improve the Celtics' long-term flexibility to build around Tatum, but next year's iteration will require the aging George to discover the fountain of youth. The 36-year-old forward has played in 60 games just once in the past seven seasons.

Even so, this shouldn't be viewed as a gap year. The Celtics return a cohesive nucleus, and they added Robinson's defense and rebounding to shore up a frontcourt rotation that was overwhelmed in the postseason.

If Tatum returns to superstar form in his first fully healthy season since a May 2025 Achilles injury, the Celtics will have a chance to win at least 50 games for the sixth straight year. Securing Banner 19, however, will likely require finding a superstar replacement for Brown sometime down the road. -- Ben Golliver

Read the full Celtics offseason recap/season preview

Brooklyn Nets: Sept. 16

Toronto Raptors: Sept. 17

New York Knicks: Sept. 18

Central Division

Milwaukee Bucks: Sept. 7
Key additions: Tyler Herro, Kel'el Ware, Jaime Jaquez Jr., Kasparas Jakucionis, Caris LeVert

Key retentions: Gary Trent Jr.

Key subtractions: Giannis Antetokounmpo, Bobby Portis

After 13 seasons, the Giannis era ended in Milwaukee with a mega trade to the Heat -- and the 2026-27 season will mark a major shift for the rebuilding franchise.

The Bucks hired coach Taylor Jenkins to establish a culture. They added four new players from Miami, including former All-Star and Wisconsin native Tyler Herro, and selected Brayden Burries with the No. 10 pick in June.

The Bucks will enter the season with an ill-fitting mix of players and low expectations, but they have the luxury to see what sticks long term. -- Jamal Collier

Read the full Bucks offseason recap/season preview

Chicago Bulls: Sept. 8
Key additions: F Caleb Wilson, G Dailyn Swain, C Nic Claxton, G Norman Powell, Tiago Splitter

Key subtractions: None

Key retentions: F Zach Collins

For years, Chicago has been seen as one of the sleeping giants of the NBA, a once-proud franchise reduced to meandering in the play-in tournament and in the middle of the lottery in recent seasons. But the Bulls got a much-needed makeover this summer and enter the 2026-27 season with a clearer direction than they've had in years.

The changes have been full-scale: Bryson Graham was hired as the team's new head of basketball operations, Tiago Splitter will patrol the sidelines as head coach, No. 4 pick Caleb Wilson is the new face of the franchise, and he'll be surrounded by some veterans like Nic Claxton and Norman Powell to help ease his transition. -- Jamal Collier

Read the full Bulls offseason recap/season preview

Cleveland Cavaliers: Sept. 9
Key additions: Peyton Watson, Mario Hezonja

Key subtractions: Dean Wade, Dennis Schroder, Max Strus, Larry Nance Jr., Caris Levert, Keon Ellis

Key retentions: Donovan Mitchell, James Harden

The Cavs' failed pursuit of LeBron James this summer turned into a pivot for a younger, athletic wing, prying Watson from the Nuggets after a career-year.

Watson averaged career highs in points, rebounds, assists and steals while shooting 41% from 3 last year, and he has in recent years been one of the strongest wing defenders in the league. That makes him a strong complement next to James Harden and Donovan Mitchell, as the Cavs hope he can provide a substantial answer to the elusive fifth starter role next to their core four. -- Jamal Collier

Read the full Cavaliers offseason recap/season preview

Detroit Pistons: Sept. 10
Key additions: John Collins, Isaiah Joe, Taurean Prince, Gary Harris

Key subtractions: Tobias Harris, Isaiah Stewart

Key retentions: None

The Pistons' offseason is still in limbo as negotiations with restricted free agent Jalen Duren have stalled.

Detroit believes it sent Duren a fair offer considering the totality of his 2025-26 season -- including his underwhelming playoff showing -- while Duren feels like he's checked off all the boxes to get more.

Losing Harris and Stewart will be a big test to their culture -- or a signal they have to win a different way than in the last two seasons.

They added shooting on the margins with Joe, Prince and Harris. And assuming Duren's deal gets done before camp, Ausar Thompson's contract is next on the docket. -- Vincent Goodwill

Read the full Pistons offseason recap/season preview

Indiana Pacers: Sept. 11
Key additions: Kelly Oubre Jr., Larry Nance Jr.

Key retentions: None

Key subtractions: C Micah Potter

The Pacers didn't make any major offseason changes, but they will have two major additions to the roster they were missing last year: starting center Ivica Zubac, who was acquired at the trade deadline from the Clippers, and star guard Tyrese Haliburton, returning from injury for the first time since the 2025 NBA Finals.

Haliburton's presence lifted the Pacers into an Eastern Conference contender in 2024 and '25, and 16 months after a torn Achilles, they'll be counting on him to do the same in 2027. And Zubac will provide a different kind of center than Myles Turner provided the last time Haliburton was on the court. -- Jamal Collier

Read the full offseason recap/season preview

Southeast Division

Miami Heat: Aug. 31
Key additions: Giannis Antetokounmpo, Klay Thompson, Bobby Portis, Tim Hardaway Jr., Nick Richards

Key retentions: Andrew Wiggins, Simone Fontecchio

Key subtractions: Tyler Herro, Norman Powell, Kel'el Ware, Jaime Jaquez Jr., Kasparas Jakucionis

Heat president Pat Riley landed the superstar he'd been searching for since LeBron James left Miami in 2016. Antetokounmpo is in the fold, and Miami is ready to contend for another title with the two-time MVP. Antetokounmpo is just as motivated to win his second title and remind everyone that he can be the best player in the league.

In the trade, the Heat gave up key players such as Herro, Ware and Jaquez and did not bring back Powell in free agency. They landed Thompson to a two-year, $13 million deal after the four-time champion sharpshooter worked out a buyout with the Dallas Mavericks. Miami also added Portis and Hardaway, but the team is still looking to bolster the roster around Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo. -- Ohm Youngmisuk

Read the full Heat offseason recap/season preview

Washington Wizards: Sept. 1
Key additions: AJ Dybantsa, Khris Middleton, Deandre Ayton, Tre Mann

Key subtractions: Cam Whitmore, D'Angelo Russell, Jaden Hardy

Key retentions: Trae Young

The Wizards got their jump on this pivotal offseason by acquiring Trae Young and Anthony Davis last season in trades.

Those were their two big moves and then came the big prize for losing 65 games last season - winning the lottery and drafting AJ Dybantsa with the first overall pick.

Ready to start winning games this season after losing 60 or more games in each of the past three years, Washington gave Young a four-year, $212 million contract. The Wizards added veterans like Khris Middleton and Deandre Ayton to bolster the depth behind their young core featuring the likes of Dybantsa, Alex Sarr, Kyshawn George, Tre Johnson and Will Riley. -- Ohm Youngmisuk

Read the full Wizards offseason recap/season preview

Charlotte Hornets: Sept. 2
Key additions: F Naz Reid, G Grayson Allen, G Dennis Schroder, F Royce O'Neale, F Dorian Finney-Smith

Key retentions: G Coby White

Key subtractions: G LaMelo Ball, F Miles Bridges, G Josh Green, G Tre Mann

After enjoying their best season in a decade, the Hornets sharply changed course with the surprising decision to trade Ball, their franchise guard, to the Timberwolves.

Given that Ball was a borderline All-Star on a max contract, Charlotte opted for a "Moneyball" approach in hopes of avoiding the perpetual mediocrity that tripped up Trae Young's Atlanta Hawks in the recent past.

With Ball and starting forward Miles Bridges moved in separate deals aimed at collecting future draft assets and improving its cap flexibility, Charlotte is now the only team that doesn't have a single player on the books for at least $25 million next season. -- Ben Golliver

Read the full Hornets offseason recap/season preview

Atlanta Hawks: Sept. 3
Key additions: Luguentz Dort, Aaron Wiggins, Kingston Flemings, Devin Carter, Ryan Nembhard, Zuby Ejiofor, Henri Veesaar

Key retentions: CJ McCollum, Jock Landale

Key subtractions: Zaccharie Risacher, Jonathan Kuminga, Gabe Vincent, Keaton Wallace

Atlanta continued to move forward from the Trae Young trade last season by being opportunistic this offseason.

The Hawks acquired Dort and Wiggins in separate trades from the Oklahoma City Thunder to add more help around emerging star Jalen Johnson. The Hawks also kept McCollum on a one-year, $21 million deal and drafted Flemings eighth overall.

Atlanta is loaded with young wings looking to take a step forward under Quin Snyder like Nickeil Alexander-Walker did last season in winning Most Improved Player. -- Ohm Youngmisuk

Read the full Hawks offseason recap/season preview

Orlando Magic: Sept. 4
Key additions: C Nikola Vucevic, G Izaiyah Nelson

Key subtractions: F Moritz Wagner, G Jett Howard

Key retentions: F Jonathan Isaac, G Jevon Carter

The Magic's biggest move this offseason was hiring Sean Sweeney to replace Jamahl Mosley.

Orlando also brought Nikola Vucevic back on a one-year, $3.9 million deal since trading him in 2021 and will use his ability to score and shoot to space the floor for Paolo Banchero, Franz Wagner and Desmond Bane.

The Magic blew a 3-1 lead over top-seeded Detroit in the first round of the playoffs after Wagner went down due to injury and were in desperate need of someone who can get easier baskets and make outside shots. Vucevic should help. Moe Wagner departed for Brooklyn via free agency, separating Franz from his brother for the first time in his pro career. -- Ohm Youngmisuk

Read the full Magic offseason recap/season preview

Pacific Division

Los Angeles Lakers: Aug. 24
Key additions: C Walker Kessler, F Sandro Mamukelashvili, G Quentin Grimes, G Collin Sexton, F Kevon Looney, F Matisse Thybulle, G Cameron Carr

Key retentions: G Austin Reaves

Key subtractions: F LeBron James, C Deandre Ayton, G Marcus Smart, F Rui Hachimura, G Luke Kennard, C Jaxson Hayes

James informed the Lakers he would not be returning for next season on June 30. Two days later, the team transformed the roster, with Doncic squarely as the focal point.

The biggest addition -- literally and figuratively -- is 7-foot-2 center Kessler, acquired in a sign-and-trade deal with the Utah Jazz. L.A. sent two unprotected first-round picks in 2031 and 2033 and pick swaps in 2028 and 2030, not to mention a four-year, $130 million contract, to acquire him.

Mamukelashvili, Grimes, Sexton, Looney and Thybulle also signed with the Lakers, and free agent Ziaire Williams and first-round pick Carr bolster the team's young prospect pool of Adou Thiero, Bronny James and Dalton Knecht.

The most important move, though, came when Reaves, coming off a career season in which he averaged 23.3 points, 4.7 rebounds and 5.5 assists per game, signed a four-year, $180 million extension.

When the dust settled, it was a dramatic roster overhaul in what could prove to be one of the most consequential summers in franchise history, with the team also being sold for the second time in 14 months, this time to venture capitalist Josh Kushner and former Disney CEO Bob Iger, who bought the Lakers from Mark Walter at a $12.5 billion valuation. -- Dave McMenamin

Read the full Lakers offseason recap/season preview

LA Clippers: Aug. 25
Key additions: Rui Hachimura, Keaton Wagler, Brandon Ingram (TBD), Gradey Dick (TBD)

Key retentions: Kobe Sanders, Bradley Beal

Key subtractions: Kawhi Leonard (TBD), Nicolas Batum, Bogdan Bogdanovic, John Collins

What started as a reconfiguration at the trade deadline -- acquiring Darius Garland from Cleveland for James Harden and Bennedict Mathurin from Indiana for Ivica Zubac -- turned into a complete overhaul this summer after the Clippers let Bogdan Bogdanovic, Nicolas Batum and John Collins walk.

Their biggest move, however, was trading Leonard to the Toronto Raptors for Brandon Ingram, Gradey Dick and draft picks, but that deal is in limbo pending the investigation into alleged salary cap circumvention by the team relating to Leonard's Aspiration endorsement deal.

In the meantime, LA added Illinois guard Wagler with the No. 5 pick in the draft and signed Hachimura away from the crosstown Lakers with a two-year, $28 million deal. And in a surprise move, Bradley Beal -- after declining his $5.6 million contract option for next season in June to test free agency -- ended up re-signing on a two-year, $13.2 million deal in mid-August to stay with the Clippers. -- Dave McMenamin

Read the full Clippers offseason recap/season preview

Golden State Warriors: Aug. 26
Key additions: Yaxel Lendeborg, Brandon Williams, Georges Niang

Key subtractions: Quinten Post, Pat Spencer

Key retentions: Draymond Green, Al Horford, Kristaps Porzingis, Gary Payton II, De'Anthony Melton

The Warriors opted for flexibility and stability over a larger shake-up around Curry. Their much-publicized recruitment of James never gained much traction.

They brought back their veteran frontcourt trio (Green, Horford, Porzingis), but kept them all on short-term maneuverable contracts. They opted for the fit of Melton over a pursuit of scoring guard Anfernee Simons. Their big addition is Lendeborg, the 23-year-old rookie wing who they will rely upon to be a high-minute, high-impact rotation player immediately.

In the bigger picture, they protected their draft pick cupboard and lined up their books to have an ocean of cap space as they peer a bit deeper into the future while their core ages. -- Anthony Slater

Read the full Warriors offseason recap/season preview

Phoenix Suns: Aug. 27
Key additions: F Miles Bridges, F Koa Peat, G Luke Kennard

Key subtractions: G Grayson Allen, F Royce O'Neale

Key retentions: F Dillon Brooks, G Collin Gillespie, C Mark Williams, G Jordan Goodwin

Phoenix followed up its surprising season with a series of moves to mostly keep its team intact, with some adjustments around the margins.

The Suns re-signed Gillespie (four years, $48 million), Williams (three years, $38 million), Goodwin (three years, $19 million) and Brooks (three years, $73 million) to new deals and made a major splash by trading Allen and O'Neale to the Charlotte Hornets for Bridges. And despite not having a pick until No. 47 in the second round of the 2026 draft, Phoenix was able to acquire Arizona player Peat -- who averaged 14.1 points on 52.8% shooting as a freshman for the Wildcats and was key to their Final Four run. -- Dave McMenamin

Read the full Suns offseason recap/season preview

Sacramento Kings: Aug. 28
Key additions: G Darius Acuff Jr., F Alex Karaban, G Emanuel Sharp

Key subtractions: G DeMar DeRozan, G Russell Westbrook

Key retentions: F Precious Achiuwa

Perry, currently in the organization's power seat, is continuing a steady transition toward the younger core he has drafted. Arkansas guard and No. 7 pick Acuff is the spotlight name on a roster populated with six players in their first two NBA seasons.

But they still have notable high-minute holdovers from the past regime, including Murray, Malik Monk, LaVine and Sabonis. Of those four, Murray appears the most locked-in as a stable member of the team's long-term vision. Perry explored trades for Monk, LaVine and Sabonis over the past year, but didn't value the proposed returns, and the three are expected to open the season in Sacramento. -- Anthony Slater

Read the full Kings offseason recap/season preview

Northwest Division

Portland Trail Blazers: Aug. 17
Key additions: G Ja Morant, F Jeremy Sochan

Key retentions: C Robert Williams III

Key subtractions: F Jerami Grant, F Kris Murray, G Matisse Thybulle

Sadly, the Blazers made far more noise this offseason with their off-court business dealings than anything they did with their roster. New owner Tom Dundon's aggressive cost-cutting measures and ongoing fight for arena financing have distracted from the progress that Portland made on the court last season, when it reached the playoffs for the first time since 2021.

Although the Blazers were the only team that sat out June's draft by not making a pick, they will add two high-profile guards to a rotation that otherwise looks very similar to last season. Lillard, a franchise icon, is back from an Achilles tendon injury that sidelined him for the entire 2025-26 campaign, and Morant, a two-time All-Star, arrived in a trade that sent Grant and Murray to the Memphis Grizzlies. -- Ben Golliver

Read the full Blazers offseason recap/season preview

Utah Jazz: Aug. 18
Key additions: G Darryn Peterson, C Jaxson Hayes, G Josh Okogie

Key retentions: C Jusuf Nurkic

Key subtractions: C Walker Kessler

The Jazz finally got some lottery luck, landing at No. 2 and taking Peterson, a gifted guard who has the potential to emerge as the face of the franchise. The hope was that Peterson would be the final major piece in Utah's rebuild, but that plan featured Kessler as the team's long-term starting center. Instead, the Jazz agreed to a sign-and-trade deal that sent Kessler to the Lakers in exchange for a pair of future first-round picks and two swaps.

The return was widely considered to be great value for Utah, particularly after Kessler's deal (four years, $130 million) pushed beyond the Jazz's comfort zone, but there is now a glaring need in the starting lineup alongside Jackson and Lauri Markkanen in the frontcourt. -- Tim MacMahon

Read the full Jazz offseason recap/season preview

Minnesota Timberwolves: Aug. 19
Key additions: G LaMelo Ball, G Josh Green, G Isaiah Evans

Key subtractions: F Julius Randle, C Naz Reid

Key retentions: G Ayo Dosunmu, G Bones Hyland, G Jaylen Clark

Wolves president of basketball operations Tim Connelly continued to show his aggression, orchestrating a four-team trade with the Brooklyn Nets, Chicago Bulls and Charlotte Hornets that sent out three-time All-Star Randle and the 2023-24 Sixth Man of the Year, Reid, and a future first-round pick to bring in the talented -- but polarizing -- Ball.

That move followed Connelly inking 6-foot-4 guard Dosunmu to a five-year, $112 million extension in June, following his acquisition at the deadline.

Minnesota also re-signed wing Clark and guard Hyland and acquired the 6-foot-6 Evans out of Duke with the No. 33 pick in the draft.

Coach Chris Finch also lost his top lieutenant on the bench, Micah Nori, who left to coach the Portland Trail Blazers. -- Dave McMenamin

Read the full Timberwolves offseason recap/season preview

Oklahoma City Thunder: Aug. 20
Key additions: C Aday Mara, G Bennett Stirtz

Key retentions: G Kenrich Williams, C Isaiah Hartenstein

Key subtractions: G Isaiah Joe, G Aaron Wiggins, G Luguentz Dort

The extensions for both Jalen Williams and Chet Holmgren triggered in July, leading to a trio of financially motivated trades to slash the tax bill and cost-control the current roster.

They sent Isaiah Joe to Detroit and traded Aaron Wiggins and Lu Dort to Atlanta in separate moves, eroding their depth.

General manager Sam Presti made clear in an interview with The Oklahoman that the impression he's been given from ownership is "the savings generated this summer, and from being out of the tax the last several years, will be re-allocated to future teams."

That would mean extra breathing room to eventually extend core young players such as Cason Wallace and Ajay Mitchell. Wallace, the likely replacement starter for Dort, is extension eligible off his rookie contract into October. -- Anthony Slater

Read the full Thunder offseason recap/season preview

Denver Nuggets: Aug. 21
Key additions: Marvin Bagley III, Lonnie Walker IV

Key retentions: Spencer Jones, Tyus Jones

Key subtractions: Watson, Tim Hardaway Jr., Jonas Valanciunas

Finding a resolution to Watson's restricted free agency was Denver's most important piece of summer business.

Watson is a draft success story, rising from the 30th overall pick into one of the league's more intriguing young two-way wings. But retaining the 23-year-old would have been expensive -- via either a sky-high luxury tax bill or a salary-slashing move to get off an important veteran and generate more breathing room for a new deal.

After Wednesday's deal to send Watson to Cleveland, Denver's front office can shift its attention to escaping the salary cap's second apron. The Nuggets are currently the league's only team above it. -- Anthony Slater

Read the full Nuggets offseason recap/season preview

Southwest Division

Memphis Grizzlies: Aug. 14
Key additions: F Cameron Boozer, G D'Angelo Russell, F Isaiah Stewart, F Jerami Grant, F Kris Murray, C Quinten Post

Key retentions: None

Key subtractions: G Ja Morant, F Santi Aldama

Memphis finally traded Ja Morant, turning the last page from an ultimately disappointing chapter in franchise history, and already has his replacement as the face of the franchise in place: No. 3 pick Cameron Boozer. GM Zach Kleiman has overhauled the roster in the past few transaction cycles, acquiring four first-round picks when he traded Desmond Bane, a few more when he dealt Jaren Jackson Jr. and none for Morant, whose departure signaled a fresh start for the Grizzlies and him.

Memphis is in a full-blown youth movement, as 21-year-old forward GG Jackson is now the longest-tenured player on the roster. The Grizzlies say they believe they have a long-term foundation in place with their last few lottery picks: center Zach Edey, small forward Cedric Coward and power forward Boozer. -- Tim MacMahon

Read the full Grizzlies offseason recap/season preview

New Orleans Pelicans: Aug. 13
Key additions: None

Key retentions: C DeAndre Jordan

Key subtractions: F Kevon Looney

Despite capturing a combined 47 wins over the last two seasons under executive vice president Joe Dumars and general manager Troy Weaver, the Pelicans clearly believe that internal growth is the best path forward. Perhaps that justifies a near-silent summer in which the hiring of new coach Jamahl Mosley turned out to be the team's most notable move. Mosley becomes New Orleans' third coach since Dumars took the helm in April 2025. In addition to drafting Jaron Pierre Jr. in the second round, New Orleans signed just two new players over the summer in Kobe Bufkin and Hunter Dickinson, while bringing back 14 of the 15 players from last season's squad. -- Michael C. Wright

Read the full Pelicans offseason recap/season preview

Dallas Mavericks: Aug. 12
Key additions: F Morez Johnson Jr., F Zaccharie Risacher

Key retentions: Moussa Cisse

Key subtractions: Khris Middleton, Ryan Nembhard

The major changes made by the Mavericks this offseason were in the managerial and coaching ranks. After a seasonlong search, team governor Patrick Dumont hired Masai Ujiri to run the franchise's basketball operations, bringing the architect of the Toronto Raptors' 2019 title team to Dallas. Ujiri decided to part ways with coach Jason Kidd and recruited Dusty May, fresh off an NCAA title with Michigan, to replace him.

Johnson, who played for May at Michigan before the Mavs selected him with the No. 9 pick in the draft, is the headliner of the additions to the roster. Dallas added three potential immediate contributors in a six-team deal, acquiring former Grizzlies forward Santi Aldama, ex-Pistons guard Marcus Sasser and EuroLeague veteran Tarik Biberovic. The franchise also landed former No. 1 pick as part of the trade that sent Luguentz Dort from the Oklahoma City Thunder to the Atlanta Hawks. -- MacMahon

Read the full Mavericks offseason recap/season preview

Houston Rockets: Aug. 11
Key additions: G Marcus Smart, G Bogdan Bogdanovic

Key retentions: F Tari Eason

Key subtractions: F Dorian Finney-Smith, G Josh Okogie

After suffering a first-round postseason exit for the second consecutive season, the Rockets resisted the temptation to jump into the Giannis Antetokounmpo sweepstakes after adding former MVP Durant last summer. General manager Rafael Stone and coach Ime Udoka will instead lean on growth from the team's collection of young talent acquired in recent years, not to mention the continuity that comes with those players developing together over multiple seasons.

Houston signed Tari Eason to a five-year, $81.5 million extension over the summer. But outside of that, the Rockets focused on bolstering depth by bringing aboard veterans Marcus Smart and Bogdan Bogdanovic. The club also brought in renowned shooting coach Chip Engelland from Oklahoma City. Engelland spent more than a decade with the San Antonio Spurs, winning two titles. -- Wright

Read the full Rockets offseason recap/season preview

San Antonio Spurs: Aug. 10
Key additions: F Tobias Harris

Key retentions: F Harrison Barnes

Key subtractions: None

San Antonio's surprising run to the NBA Finals never obscured its long-term vision for building a sustainable competitor around Victor Wembanyama. Clearly, the Frenchman views the future similarly, considering he signed a 25% max extension worth $252 million instead of the available 30% supermax escalators that would've rocketed the contract to $303 million.

Wembanyama did it to keep San Antonio's talented young core together for as long as possible, with added flexibility to acquire needed supporting players. The Spurs grabbed one of those in free agency in Harris, an experienced, reliable scorer who adds size (6-foot-8, 226 pounds) and physicality on defense while bolstering frontcourt depth in the draft. -- Wright

stories.headline: Fantasy hockey draft picks: Grab these defensemen before their breakout year
stories.summary: Everyone's looking for a breakout season before it happens. Here are the defensemen with the right opportunities.
stories.body:
Darren Raddysh is the exception, not the rule. He's not what we are looking for. A 30-year-old defender launching from 1.32 fantasy points per game to 2.29 fantasy points per game happens about as often as a leap year. What we are after is what happens more often. We are leaning into the "usual."

As in, usually "a defenseman has played X number of games and are usually X years old when they start to contribute to fantasy hockey."

Here's the quick line to what I'm defining as "usual."

The median fantasy points per game (FPPG) across the 1,020 individual top-60 defense seasons since 2009-10 is 1.89, so that's the bar we set for a breakout.

Using all game logs since the 2009-10 season, there are 162 defenders that have made more than one appearance among the top 60 for fantasy scoring. This purposefully excludes any one-time flukes.

Of those 162 defenders, 98 made their debut in 2009-10 or later, meaning we have complete game logs for their entire career.

Of those 98 defenders, 73 eventually held a rolling 41-game FPPG average above 1.89 for at least 41 consecutive games -- a half-season at that pace at minimum, and often longer.

The average age those 73 blue-liners had reached when that breakout run began was 24 years, 248 days (with the majority doing it between 22 years, 330 days and 26 years, 266 days).

The average experience those 73 D had when that run began was 254 games played (with the majority doing it between 157 and 379).

So Raddysh is unusual.

He didn't make the list of 73 because he hasn't had multiple top-60 fantasy seasons. He will after this season, but that's not the point. The point is that only a half a dozen D-men since the 2009-10 season have burst onto the scene when they are as old as Raddysh. By the numbers, we want to look for younger players when hoping for a breakout.

What's interesting though is when you consider the other half of the formula: Experience.

Raddysh has a career 249 games played, which is only five games shy of the "usual" breakout experience for the 73 defenders that made the breakout list. Age is important, but it clearly isn't the only factor. Raddysh didn't make his debut until he was 25 and didn't play his first full season until he was 27.

So we flip Raddysh's profile around. Instead of a player who arrived late and spiked out of nowhere, we're hunting the defenders sitting right in that pocket. Young enough that the breakout is probably still ahead of them, experienced enough that they're due. And to keep this list actually useful, I've thrown out anyone who's already posted a top-60 fantasy season on the blue line. We're not looking for guys who've done it before; we're looking for the ones who haven't done it yet.

More: Sign up for free | Rankings | Projections | League types

The breakouts

Philip Broberg, D, St. Louis Blues (25.2 years old, 1.14 FPPG in 230 games played): Broberg is already a heavy-minutes, underlying-metrics darling and the only thing capping his fantasy value is a power play he's never truly run. With Justin Faulk now in Detroit, that quarterback job is finally open. Win it over Logan Mailloux and the 50-point breakout arrives; lose it and he's a multi-category floor play.

Jamie Drysdale, D, Philadelphia Flyers (24.4 years old, 1.23 FPPG in 295 games played): Drysdale took a step last season (32 points), got a new four-year deal for it, and opens 2026-27 quarterbacking Philadelphia's top power play. The 50-point ceiling is live if he seizes true top-pairing minutes. The recurring "if" is health, which has interrupted every prior run at a breakout.

Owen Power, D, Buffalo Sabres (23.8 years old, 1.39 FPPG in 323 games played): The former No. 1 pick has the pedigree and the minutes but keeps refusing to shoot, as he managed zero power-play points last season despite getting 75 minutes there. Power has shown he can play defense, the key will be him deciding to chip in on offense once in a while, too.

Luke Hughes, D, New Jersey Devils (23.0 years old, 1.39 FPPG in 223 games played): Even splitting the top power play with Dougie Hamilton, Hughes ranked 14th among qualified defensemen (minimum 1:15 per game) in power-play points per 60 last season -- elite rate production that just needs more time to become raw totals. Hamilton keeps it a committee, but the per-minute scoring says Hughes doesn't need the whole job to pay off.

Pavel Mintyukov, D, Anaheim Ducks (22.8 years old, 1.33 FPPG in 204 games played): Anaheim bet five years and $36 million on Mintyukov's upside, and a rising even-strength role should push him past 20 minutes a night with triple-digit blocks and shots. The catch is the power play. Jackson LaCombe owns the top unit, so unless Mintyukov pries it loose, his point ceiling stays capped and he's more floor than fireworks.

J.J. Moser, D, Tampa Bay Lightning (26.2 years old, 1.34 FPPG in 338 games played): Fittingly, Moser spent last season paired with the very same Darren Raddysh from our intro, the two forming one of the NHL's stingiest shutdown duos. He'll get to run it back this year as the shutdown side of the top pairing with either Victor Hedman or John Carlson. The question now is whether he can layer the shot-blocking and hits from his Coyotes days back onto the big minutes and points he's found in Tampa.

ESPN Fantasy Hockey is the fun, free way to get inside the game. Draft your players, set your lineups and earn points when the pros do. Sign up today!

Already broken out

These defenders already cracked the top 60 in a season, so they're not breakouts in the strict sense, but they sit right in the same age-and-experience wheelhouse as the names above. Several are still going under-appreciated on draft day relative to what they already produce. Consider them the safer, proven cousins of the bets we just made.

Bowen Byram, D, Chicago Blackhawks (25.2 years old, 1.46 FPPG in 331 games played): Byram's move to Chicago gives him a real shot at the offensive keys he could never fully hold in Buffalo or Colorado. Just know he'll have to hold off the young Blackhawks blue line for the power-play reps. The counting stats are proven, but the top-unit role isn't handed to him.

Mattias Samuelsson, D, Buffalo Sabres (26.5 years old, 2.01 FPPG in 292 games played): Ignore the shiny plus-41 that inflated last year's rate, it won't repeat, and it's an increasingly rare fantasy category anyway. The reason to roster Samuelsson is the floor beneath it, as he led the Sabres in blocked shots and ranked among their top hitters. This is the kind of every-night volume that quietly wins the peripheral categories a lot of managers punt.

Brandt Clarke, D, Los Angeles Kings (23.6 years old, 2.02 FPPG in 188 games played): Clarke is the youngest name here and the most complete offensive package. The 23-year-old is a legitimate power-play performer already producing at a top-tier rate, and now stepping fully out of Drew Doughty's shadow to run the Kings' back end as his own.

Simon Edvinsson, D, Detroit Red Wings (23.6 years old, 1.77 FPPG in 177 games played): Two of the 60 most physical seasons any defenseman 23-or-younger has posted since 2009-10 belong to Edvinsson, and he's played only two full ones, with his workload still climbing. He pairs with Moritz Seider, a star in his own right who tops that very list, giving Detroit a young shutdown tandem that already floods the hits-and-blocks columns; the points will follow as the minutes do.

Braden Schneider, D, New York Rangers (24.9 years old, 1.42 FPPG in 372 games played): Schneider turns up on that same list as Edvinsson -- one of the most physical young-defenseman seasons since 2009-10 -- which is the whole case for him: hits, blocks, and a quietly growing point total that add up to more than the zero fantasy buzz he gets behind the Rangers' bigger names. He won't win you a category, but he's the steady multi-cat piece that outproduces his draft slot.

stories.headline: Messi tracker: Goals, assists, key moments in 2026
stories.summary: ESPN provides game-by-game analysis of Lionel Messi's performances for Inter Miami and Argentina.
stories.body:
Lionel Messi will aim for more success in 2026. His Inter Miami side captured its first MLS Cup title last season and will look to defend it -- and add further silverware too -- in its first season at Nu Stadium, the club's new home.

Messi also captained Argentina as they fell just one step short of defending their FIFA World Cup crown, losing 1-0 in extra time to Spain in the final of what could be his last tournament.

As the 39-year-old continues to feature for both club and country, ESPN will track his performances game-by-game, providing stats and analysis each time he pulls on a Herons or Albiceleste jersey.

Messi's 2026 tally:

Games played: 36
Goals: 32
Assists: 14

Sep. 12: Inter Miami 2-2 Nashville SC
In a matchup between the two best teams in the Eastern Conference, the action went end to end, with Messi getting on the scoresheet for Miami's second goal off a Rodrigo De Paul assist as he continues to lead the Golden Boot race.

Ultimately, the teams settled for a point apiece, as the hosts failed to close the gap on Nashville at the top of the table.

Sep. 9: Chicago Fire 1-1 Inter Miami

Two or Europe's greatest club players took center stage in one of the United States' most iconic American football stadiums on Wednesday -- and a record crowd came out to watch.

Ex-Bayern Munich and Barcelona star Robert Lewandowski scored a trademark acrobatic goal in the 10th minute to give the Fire an early lead at the NFL home of the Chicago Bears.

But Inter Miami drew level shortly after halftime when Casemiro, another of the game's stars with a long history of playing in Europe before moving to MLS, headed home a Messi cross from a corner kick to make it 1-1.

The assist was Messi's league-leading 13th of the season. He also has league 18 goals and is the first player in MLS history with 30-plus goal contributions in three separate seasons.

Sep. 5: Inter Miami 2-2 Atlanta United
Messi was not as effective as he was in the previous matchup, but he did get an assist for Casemiro's opening goal. However, his team was unable to win as they had to settle for a point in a 2-2 draw.

August 29: Inter Miami 7-1 CF Montréal

Fans were treated to a Messi masterclass on Saturday as the Argentine magician registered four goals and an assist to help Miami to a club-record 7-1 victory over CF Montréal.

Messi scored with a deflected free kick in the 40th minute before netting after a stunning solo run in the 52nd. After supplying an assist to Luis Suárez, the 39-year-old then completed his hat trick and with a delicate chip over the goalkeeper with seven minutes of regulation time remaining.

He wasn't done yet.

Deep into stoppage time, Messi lined up a free kick and dispatched it with trademark precision into the top corner of the net. Legendary stuff.

August 22: Inter Miami 2-1 Toronto FC

Messi's 14th MLS goal of the season wasn't enough to prevent Inter Miami from slumping to their fourth loss in their last five games, losing 2-1 to Toronto FC at Nu Stadium on Saturday.

Messi found the net with a first-time finish from a Rodrigo De Paul through-ball with eight minutes remaining, but the home side's late rally fell short of salvaging a much-needed draw to bolster the Herons' pursuit of first-placed Nashville SC in the Eastern Conference.

August 19: Inter Miami 2-2 Philadelphia Union

Messi is back scoring goals, but unfortunately, his Miami side is not back to winning ways. The Argentine scored Miami's second goal of the night as both teams finished with 10 men. Miami are now winless in their last four matches.

August 15: Nashville SC 4-1 Inter Miami
It was not the best night for Messi in Tennessee. The Argentine missed yet another penalty -- his third straight for club and country -- and they suffered a heavy 4-1 loss to their Eastern Conference rivals. However, he did get an assist for Telasco Segovia's equalizer at halftime before Miami lost control in the second half.

August 12: Inter Miami 2-3 Club León
Just days after the passing of his father, Messi came off the bench in the second half to try to help Miami continue in the Leagues Cup after they were leading 1-0. However, it ended in a 3-2 loss which saw them eliminated in the league phase after a second straight loss, coming off defeat to Monterrey last weekend with Messi away at the memorial for his father.

August 5: Inter Miami 4-2 Atlético de San Luis

Lionel Messi made his first start for Inter Miami since returning from the World Cup and picked up right where he left off, scoring a stellar pair of goals to guide his team to a come-from-behind 4-2 rout of Atlético de San Luis in its first game of the 2026 Leagues Cup.

Messi's first goal was an exquisite volley, redirecting Noah Allen's cross from the left flank while running at full speed. Miami's third goal of the opening half -- and Messi's second on the night -- came on the back of some intricate buildup play with Allen once again setting up his team captain, this time in the center of the area where he tiptoed through two defenders and buried a close-range strike past Andrés Sánchez.

The goal made Messi the all-time leading scorer in Leagues Cup history with 14, one ahead of LAFC's Denis Bouanga since the expanded competition began in 2023.

August 1: Inter Miami 2-2 Columbus Crew
Messi made his return to action for Inter Miami on Saturday, 13 days after tasting defeat with Argentina in the World Cup final. The Miami talisman started on the substitutes' bench before being introduced in the 53rd minute of the Herons' 2-2 draw with the Columbus Crew at Nu Stadium in Miami.

July 19: Spain 1-0 AET Argentina

Sunday proved to be a bridge too far for both Messi and Argentina, falling in extra time to Spain in the World Cup final.

With La Roja controlling the match basically from start to finish -- Argentina didn't register a shot on target during regulation time -- Messi had few opportunities to impact the game. Indeed, the 39-year-old was given a 3/10 in ESPN's post-match player ratings.

Still, as Mark Ogden points out, the 2026 tournament was a memorable one for Messi and cemented his status as the GOAT, if it were ever in doubt.

July 15: England 1-2 Argentina
Messi made another statement in his 205th appearance for Argentina, this time in his first-ever match against England in a World Cup semifinal. With so much at stake for both nations, Messi once again proved decisive despite not getting on the scoresheet.

He first provided the assist for Enzo Fernández's superb strike to level the match in the second half before delivering a pinpoint cross for Lautaro Martínez's headed winner, sending the reigning champions into yet another World Cup final after another dramatic encounter.

Messi has now recorded either a goal or an assist in all seven of Argentina's matches at this World Cup, and he will have the opportunity to lift the trophy for a second time when Argentina face Spain in Sunday's final in New Jersey.

July 11: Argentina 3-1 Switzerland
It was a relatively quiet night by Messi's standards as his goalscoring streak came to an end, but his influence on the match stayed the same. He set up Alexis Mac Allister's opening goal for Argentina against Switzerland, and although the match went to extra time, the defending champions won 3-1 thanks to two late goals in the second half of extra time.

Messi's quest to retain the World Cup now continues into the semifinals, where Argentina will face England for the first time in over 20 years. The clash in Atlanta -- one of international soccer's most storied rivalries -- will decide a spot in the final.

July 7: Argentina 3-2 Egypt
It was another dramatic outing for Messi and Argentina, who rallied from a 2-0 deficit to defeat Egypt 3-2 in Atlanta and book their place in the World Cup quarterfinals. As is so often the case, Messi was at the center of the action. Minutes after Egypt opened the scoring, he missed another penalty, but he quickly made amends by setting up Cristian Romero for Argentina's first goal. Messi then scored the equalizer -- his eighth goal of the tournament -- before Enzo Fernández completed the comeback with the winner. Argentina will now face Switzerland in Kansas City for a place in the semifinals.

July 3: Argentina 3-2 Cape Verde
Messi suffered a major scare in Miami Gardens on Friday evening in the round of 32, but it ultimately ended well for Argentina. He opened the scoring with his seventh goal of the tournament, extending his World Cup tally to 20 goals while finding the net in a record eighth consecutive World Cup match. Cape Verde twice fought back -- once in the second half and again in extra time -- but the world champions eventually prevailed 3-2 after extra time to book a meeting in the round of 16 with Egypt.

June 27: Jordan 1-3 Argentina
Messi didn't play the full 90 minutes in Argentina's 3-1 win over an already-eliminated Jordan, but he still made his mark during a 30-minute cameo in Texas. The 39-year-old scored a free kick for his sixth goal of the tournament and his 19th career World Cup goal, becoming the first player ever to score in seven consecutive World Cup matches. Even at 39, he's still got it.

June 22: Argentina 2-0 Austria
Another chapter in an already unparalleled career. Lionel Messi scored twice in Argentina's 2-0 win over Austria to help his team qualify for the round of 32 and become the outright leading goalscorer in men's and women's FIFA World Cup history with 18 goals. After missing an early penalty, he responded by breaking Miroslav Klose's 12-year-old record and then added a second late on to break Marta's record. All just two days before turning 39.

June 16: Argentina 3-0 Algeria
In his 200th appearance for Argentina and sixth World Cup, Lionel Messi sent a message to the world just days before his 39th birthday: he still has it. His first-ever World Cup hat trick powered Argentina to victory in their group-stage opener, while his 16th tournament goal saw him draw level with Miroslav Klose for the most goals in World Cup history.

June 9: Argentina 3-0 Iceland

Messi, working his way back from muscle fatigue ahead of the start of the World Cup, came on in the 70th minute of a pre-tournament friendly in Auburn, Alabama and scored from the penalty spot right afterward.

It was Messi's 911th career goal for club and country and 117th goal for Argentina and made him the oldest scorer in the country's soccer history.

May 24: Inter Miami 6-4 Philadelphia Union

Messi registered two assists in a scintillating performance against Philadelphia on Sunday but, unfortunately, no one was focused on results come the end of the game.

That's because, in the very last game before the World Cup, Messi left the field in the 73rd minute and headed straight to the locker room after grabbing his left thigh.

Now, supporters around the world are holding their collective breath while they wait and see if the injury has scuppered the 38-year-old's chance of appearing at a sixth World Cup.

May 13: FC Cincinnati 3-5 Inter Miami

Two goals and one assist marked yet another spectacular contribution from Miami superstar Messi on Wednesday. The Argentine magician was instrumental as the Herons fought back from 3-2 down to eventually beat Cincinnati 5-3 at TQL Stadium in Ohio.

May 9: Toronto FC 2-4 Inter Miami

It was a day of star power. Not only were Rodrigo De Paul, Luis Suárez and Sergio Reguilón all on the score sheet for the Herons, so was Messi -- and he added a pair of assists, too.

While Miami has yet to taste victory at its new home, it continues to take care of business on the road. Saturday's win in Toronto extended the club's unbeaten record away from home in 2026 to seven games, picking up six wins and one draw in the first few months of the season.

May 2: Inter Miami 3-4 Orlando City

Messi notched a goal and an assist on Saturday in what ended up being an astonishing collapse for Inter Miami at Nu Stadium.

The Herons were leading 3-0 after Messi's classy 33rd-minute strike, but gifted the visitors four goals -- including a Martín Ojeda hat trick -- to once again miss out on a victory at their new home ground. Orlando's comeback from three goals down marks only the third time in MLS history that a team has claimed all three points after trailing by three or more goals.

As for Messi's Miami, only twice has an MLS team had a longer winless run -- now up to four for the Herons -- to open up a new stadium.

April 25: Inter Miami 1-1 New England Revolution
Messi again failed to get on the scoresheet as Miami put in a fatigued second-half performance that saw them come from a goal down against New England. It was another draw -- and another game without a win at their new home, Nu Stadium.

April 22: Real Salt Lake 0-2 Inter Miami
No goals or assists from Messi as Miami visited America First Field on Wednesday, but the fans did get treated to sumptuous strikes nonetheless.

Rodrigo De Paul's opener in the 80th-minute was stunning curler from outside the box and then, almost immediately after the restart, Luis Suarez made it 2-0 with a well-struck volley.

The victory moves Inter Miami into outright second in the MLS Eastern Conference.

April 18: Colorado Rapids 2-3 Inter Miami

Another moment of Messi magic bagged all three points for Inter Miami on Saturday.

With scores level in the 79th minute, the Argentine icon danced his way past a number of Colorado defenders before curling home an outrageous effort into the far corner.

The strike -- Messi's second of the match after converting a penalty in the first half -- helped Miami to their first win under interim coach Guillermo Hoyos.

Hoyos, who had been serving as club's sporting director, took over coaching duties after Javier Mascherano unexpectedly left the club due to personal reasons last week.

April 11: Inter Miami 2-2 Red Bull New York
Miami and Messi are still waiting for a first win at Nu Stadium after a 2-2 draw with Red Bull New York on Saturday night.

Messi didn't register a goal or assist, but did help set up Germán Berterame's second-half strike that gave Inter Miami its first lead at its new home ground, but 17-year-old Adri Mehmeti's first career goal in the 77th minute secured a point for the visitors.

April 4: Inter Miami 2-2 Austin FC
Inter Miami opened Nu Stadium the only way it knows how: With a Messi goal. The No. 10 began the move in trademark style with a left-footed pass to a teammate before moving past a defender and arriving in the box at just the right time to head past goalkeeper Brad Stuver.

March 31: Argentina 5-0 Zambia
It was the last day of the month and perhaps the last game for Messi playing for Argentina playing in his native country, but they put on a show defeating the African side Zambia 5-0. Messi scored the second goal for Lionel Scaloni's side as focus will shift now to Miami until the beginning of the World Cup.

March 27: Argentina 2-1 Mauritania
In his first game for his country in 2026, Messi only played the second half as Argentina won 2-1 against Mauritania at the mythical La Bombonera in Buenos Aires, as the World Cup champions continue to prepare to defend their title this summer in North America.

March 22: NYCFC 2-3 Inter Miami

It was a thrilling encounter in the Bronx, as the Argentine star helped his team to a 3-2 win over NYCFC, which also included another trademark free kick goal, now beginning his course for potentially 1,000 career goals. Only 99 goals left!

March 18: Inter Miami 1-1 Nashville SC

Messi may have made history on Wednesday night, becoming just the second men's player in history to score 900 career goals, but it wasn't enough to seal Miami's progress in the Concacaf Champions Cup.

The Argentina legend found the back of the net in the seventh minute at Chase Stadium, but his strike was cancelled out by Nashville's Cristian Espinoza -- sealing the Herons' tournament exit on the away goals rule.

March 11: Nashville SC 0-0 Inter Miami
A drab night for Messi and Co. in the Concacaf Champions Cup. Plenty of possession but few shots on target mean that the Herons will return to Chase Stadium know a win will be needed to ensure progression.

March 7: D.C. United 1-2 Inter Miami

It was quite an eventful week for Messi. Just days before Miami's match against D.C. United, Messi and the entire squad visited the White House and met President Donald Trump and were eager to put on a show for the sold-out crowd of over 70,000 at Baltimore's M&T Bank Stadium.

And they did just that, with a 2-1 win over D.C. United. Messi, of course, scored Miami's second and is now one goal away from 900 career goals.

March 1: Orlando City 2-4 Inter Miami

Well, that blip didn't last long! Messi and Miami roared back into life with a 4-2 thrashing of Orlando on Sunday thanks to the 38-year-old's wizardry.

Things looked ominous for the Herons after the first 45 minutes, down 2-0 and looking on course to start the MLS season with two bleak losses.

But two goals and an assist from Messi in the second half dragged the visitors back in the game and helped secure Miami their first points of the season.

Feb. 21: LAFC 3-0 Inter Miami
Messi and Miami aimed to start 2026 firing on all cylinders, but it was the hosts who spoiled the defending MLS Cup champions' opener at the LA Coliseum. In front of a sellout crowd of 75,673 -- the second-highest attendance in MLS history -- Miami were outplayed, with LAFC's Denis Bouanga getting a goal and an assist in a convincing home victory.

The main talking point, however, emerged after the final whistle. Messi was initially reported to have gained unauthorized access to the officials' locker room after video circulated showing him near the area. However, it was later reported that no league policy had been violated and Messi was cleared of any wrongdoing. Miami will now turn its attention next weekend against fellow Florida side Orlando City.

stories.headline: Dolphins boss opens up on contract puzzle
stories.summary: Dolphins CEO Terry Reader is calm about the big stars set to come off contract as the club gets its salary cap in balance to cope with potential raids.
stories.body:
The Dolphins have a suite of superstars set to come off contract but CEO Terry Reader has pointed to the reasons why the club remains confident of retaining the majority.

Ahead of their preliminary final with either the Sydney Roosters or Cronulla, the Dolphins have 14 players who will become free agents on November 1, including big name backline stars Herbie Farnworth, Hamiso Tabuai-Fidow, Selwyn Cobbo and Jack Bostock.

There is a saying in the NRL "you can't keep them all" and what is often overlooked in the Dolphins case is the club will farewell backline trio Jake Averillo (Wests Tigers), Jamayne Isaako (Melbourne) and Kodi Nikorima (St George Illawarra) at season's end.

Elite prop Daniel Saifiti has medically retired and will be off the salary cap books for next year, while second-rower Oryn Keeley left mid-season for the Storm.

Farnworth, who was man of the match in the 26-16 qualifying-final win, is now regarded as the best centre in the world and has constantly been linked to a Sydney Roosters switch.

"The key thing on Herbie is that all this noise was around last year, and he re-signed as well," Reader said.

"He's given us no indication, he or his management, that he'll be going anywhere. He's focused on winning a premiership .... and in his words 'winning a World Cup with England' as well.

"There is nothing to make us think what we're hearing (about the Roosters) has got any legs."

Farnworth told AAP he will put extension talks off until the end of the season and has said on several occasions remaining a Dolphin was a priority. He has rubbished the noise around him joining the Sydney Roosters.

Dolphins players have spoken about sticking together in a strong cultural environment and taking less to constantly challenge for a premiership. On top of the five players that will be off the books in 2027, the Dolphins will elevate their development list players into the top 30 which will balance their salary cap spend.

"Herbie, along with the number of players where they've got coming off contract, are wonderful players," Reader said.

"But if you look at the players that are leaving our club this year as well and the players that are coming through to get the balance right ... we're in a position to be able to keep the majority of those players."

Reader said the figures getting thrown about with regards to Dolphins players were "exaggerated" but with the ratchet clauses from the new salary cap in 2028 onwards players would be looking at approximately an extra 20 per cent per season.

With 12 of the current playing 19 all in the top 30 during the foundation season, Reader made the point those who stay would still be well rewarded and have the opportunity to challenge for titles.

"A lot of them debuted together and the nucleus of that side have an opportunity to (win competitions)," Reader said.

"If everyone wants the most they could possibly get at a different club, then the club won't be able to match that.

"Where the salary cap's going and ratchets they're all going to be very well paid men.

"It's the value they put on playing together and staying together. Penrith have won four premierships and been a dominant club for the last six to seven years with a key nucleus.

"And that's still our intention ... that we'll be able to hold onto hopefully all of them."
